hard_case_evaluation.run_note: INVALID AS A HEADLINE NUMBER - READ BEFORE QUOTING. Two problems. (1) The run was cut short: the Groq free tier 200,000 tokens-per-day ceiling was exhausted partway through, so 10 of the 34 cases returned HTTP 429 and 2 more were truncated/unparseable. Those 12 are excluded from the denominator because a call that never returned is our infrastructure failing, not the model being wrong - leaving only 22 scored cases. (2) More importantly, on those 22 the LLM scored 0.500 while simply always guessing the commonest label in the sample scores 0.864. The sample is selected by "the rule baseline was wrong", the baseline errs asymmetrically, and that skews the label mix 19:3. The constant guess is not a real rival system - it exploits the selection and would be useless on the true distribution - but the model failing to beat it means this run does NOT demonstrate the LLM recovering the baseline failures. Re-run when the daily quota resets; reasoning_effort=low now cuts token spend so a full run fits the budget.
